extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of gasoline distribution facilities and bulk gasoline terminals; state and federal air regulators; regulated industry compliance managers; environmental counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and compliance criteria for National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants (NESHAP) for gasoline distribution facilities and New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) for bulk gasoline terminals, including emissions limits, monitoring, testing, reporting, and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduated vapor tightness certification for gasoline cargo tanks
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement of a graduated vapor tightness certification from 0.5 to 1.25 inches of water pressure drop over a 5-minute period, depending on the cargo tank compartment size for gasoline cargo tanks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized across NESHAP Subpart R, NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB, and NSPS Subpart XXa; certification level depends on cargo tank compartment size. Used to demonstrate cargo tank vapor tightness during loading/unloading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitting controls for external floating roof tanks
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement of fitting controls for external floating roof tanks consistent with the requirements in 40 CFR part 60, subpart Kb (NSPS subpart Kb).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External floating roof tank control requirements in the gasoline distribution NESHAPs are aligned with existing NSPS subpart Kb specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual instrument monitoring for equipment leaks at major sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement of semiannual instrument monitoring for equipment leaks at major source gasoline distribution facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to facilities subject to NESHAP Subpart R (major sources); instrument-based leak detection frequency: twice per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual instrument monitoring for equipment leaks at area sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement of annual instrument monitoring for equipment leaks at area source gasoline distribution facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to facilities subject to NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB (area sources); instrument-based leak detection frequency: once per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly instrument monitoring for equipment leaks under NSPS Subpart XXa
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement of quarterly instrument monitoring for equipment leaks for affected facilities under NSPS Subpart XXa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to facilities that commence construction, modification, or reconstruction after June 10, 2022 (NSPS Subpart XXa). Frequency: every quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area source TOC emission limit (35 mg/L) for large bulk gasoline terminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalizing an area source emission limit of 35 milligrams of total organic carbon (TOC) per liter of gasoline loaded (mg/L) at large bulk gasoline terminals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to large bulk gasoline terminals covered by NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB; used as a performance limit for loading operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor balancing requirement for certain bulk gasoline plants
rubrics_metrics.description: Vapor balancing requirements for loading storage vessels and gasoline cargo tanks at bulk gasoline plants with actual throughput of 4,000 gallons per day or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When throughput threshold (4,000 gpd) is met, displaced vapors from cargo tanks must be captured and routed through piping back to a storage vessel (vapor balancing).

rubrics_metrics.name: NSPS Subpart XXa TOC emission limits for loading operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For loading operations under NSPS Subpart XXa: new facilities must meet a 1.0 mg/L TOC emission limit and modified and reconstructed facilities must meet a 10 mg/L TOC emission limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOC limits vary by facility vintage: more stringent for newly constructed facilities; less stringent for modified/reconstructed sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of SSM exemption in NESHAP Subpart R and related SSM revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Elimination of the SSM (startup, shutdown, and malfunction) exemption in NESHAP Subpart R; revisions to address SSM provisions in NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB; and finalizing NSPS Subpart XXa without SSM exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards are intended to apply at all times; SSM exemptions removed so emissions limits/requirements apply during SSM periods unless otherwise specified in the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding requirements for electronic reporting (e.g., via EPA tools such as ERT and CEDRI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications, performance test results, CMS data, and other required reports may need to be submitted electronically per the finalized rule and referenced EPA electronic reporting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions to monitoring and operating requirements for control devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Revising monitoring and operating requirements for control devices used to comply with the standards (general revisions across affected subparts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes updated monitoring frequencies, parametric monitoring, and operating requirements to ensure control devices operate effectively; specifics are provided in subpart regulatory text and preamble rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability criteria by facility type and construction/modification date
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability of requirements based on source category and construction/modification dates: NESHAP Subpart R applies to bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations (major sources); NESHAP Subpart BBBBBB applies to bulk gasoline terminals, bulk gasoline plants, and pipeline facilities (area sources); NSPS Subpart XX applies to terminals commenced construction/modification on or before June 10, 2022; NSPS Subpart XXa applies to those after June 10, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must examine the applicability criteria in the appropriate NESHAP/NSPS and consult EPA/State contacts to determine applicability to a particular entity. NAICS codes provided as guidance: 324110, 493190, 486910, 424710.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates for existing and new sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule effective date is July 8, 2024; existing source standards for NESHAP Subparts R and BBBBBB require compliance 3 years after promulgation (major impacts assumed to begin in 2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different compliance timelines may apply by subpart and source vintage. Regulatory Impact Analysis assumes most compliance costs and emissions reductions begin in 2027 due to the 3‑year compliance period for existing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for loading racks (NSPS and NESHAP reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule addresses standards for loading racks including proposed affected facility definitions, proposed emission limits, proposed monitoring requirements, and VRU (vapor recovery unit) operation to minimize air intrusion; rationale provided for final approach under NSPS Subpart XXa and NESHAP Subparts R/BBBBBB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble contains EPA responses to key comments on loading rack standards and the technical rationale for the selected emission limits and monitoring approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for cargo tank vapor tightness (multiple subparts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology review and NSPS review changes for gasoline cargo tanks at major and area sources and new/modified/reconstructed bulk gasoline terminals; includes the graduated vapor tightness certification requirement and rationale for final approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble sections compare proposed vs. final approaches, summarize comments received, and explain EPA's technical basis for certification levels and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for gasoline storage vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology review changes and final decisions for gasoline storage vessels at major and area sources, including fitting controls and other control options evaluated in the RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final requirements align certain storage vessel controls with NSPS subpart Kb and include applicability and technical justification in the preamble and regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for equipment leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Final monitoring and control requirements for equipment leaks across NESHAP Subparts R and BBBBBB and NSPS Subpart XXa (including required monitoring frequencies, instrument use, and LDAR approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble summarizes the required monitoring frequency by source type and provides EPA responses to comments on equipment leak approaches (e.g., use of OGI vs. instrument monitoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance testing requirements (§63.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial performance testing: dates and requirements including conducting performance testing 180 days after compliance date; three test runs of at least 1 hour each; compliance based on the arithmetic mean of three runs; reporting of raw data and performance test reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of performance test required 60 days before test; site-specific QA/test plans must be submitted 60 days before the test; performance test data must be submitted within 60 days after end of test and retained for 5 years. Force majeure and waiver provisions available under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring system operation, maintenance, and quality control (CMS/COMS) (§63.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for continuous monitoring systems (CMS) and continuous opacity monitoring systems (COMS): must be installed to get representative measurements, verified operational status before/at performance test, maintained under good air pollution control practices, and subject to performance specifications and quality control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS quality control, performance evaluations, calibration, and recordkeeping requirements apply. COMS data can be used instead of EPA Method 9 under conditions; averaging times and data reduction rules (e.g., COMS 6-minute averages) specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, reporting, and electronic submission requirements (§63.9 and §63.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must submit initial notifications, notification of performance tests, notification of startup, notification of intent to construct/reconstruct, notification of VE/opacity tests, notification related to CMS performance evaluations, and notification of compliance status; reporting and recordkeeping requirements include progress reports, excess emissions reports, and submission timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deadlines: e.g., notify Administrator 60 days before performance test; notification of VE/opacity tests 30 days prior where applicable; Notification of Compliance Status due 60 days after end of performance test (30 days for opacity/VE). Electronic reporting procedures are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping retention and content requirements (§63.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: General recordkeeping: keep all records readily available and retain for 5 years; maintain maintenance records for air pollution control and monitoring equipment; retain CMS quality control and performance evaluation records; documentation supporting notifications and compliance status must be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records related to SSM occurrences, malfunctions, and actions taken may have specific provisions in subpart text; CMS specific recordkeeping requirements apply as specified in the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative test/monitoring methods and alternative standards procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures by which the Administrator can grant approval to use alternative test methods, alternative monitoring, alternative relative accuracy tests, or to grant an alternative standard (§63.7(g), §63.8(f), §63.6(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators may seek approval for alternatives, but must follow submission procedures and get Administrator approval before relying on alternatives for compliance demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of tests and compliance extensions (§63.7, §63.6(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and criteria for waiving performance tests and for requesting compliance extensions when a source cannot meet the compliance date or has installed the best available control technology or LAER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must follow specified procedures; progress reports are required when under a compliance extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of opacity/visible emissions methods and COMS data in compliance determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a standard does not state a test method, use EPA Method 9 for opacity and EPA Method 22 for VE; COMS data can be submitted instead of Method 9 under conditions but COMS is probable (not conclusive) evidence of compliance unless COMS meet performance specs and proper QA/QC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COMS data must be reduced to 6-minute averages for performance tests; Administrator will consider all evidence (COMS, Method 9, Method 22, operation and maintenance info) when determining compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of enforcement authority to States (§63.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: State authority to enforce standards is recognized; delegation procedures for states to administer/enforce the NESHAP provisions are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators should coordinate with their delegated State air agency for reporting and enforcement expectations where delegation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of test methods and appendices (§63.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test methods and specifications referred to in the subparts are incorporated by reference (e.g., EPA methods in appendices to parts 60 and 63).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must use the referenced methods unless an alternative is approved by the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and benefits analysis guidance for chosen standards
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducted a Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) to estimate emissions reductions, costs, and monetized benefits (including health benefits and climate disbenefits) for the final action; analyses considered baseline, less stringent, and more stringent options and used 2027–2041 projection period with PV/EAV in 2021 dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA methodology details (base year, discounting, interest rates, product recovery valuation, model plants) and assumptions are provided in the supporting RIA documents in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice and other statutory/executive order reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducted analyses required under various statutes and Executive Orders (e.g., E.O. 12866/14094, Paperwork Reduction Act, Regulatory Flexibility Act, Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, Executive Orders on federalism, tribal consultation, children’s health, energy effects, NTTAA, E.O.12898/E.O.14096 on environmental justice) as part of the rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble summarizes EPA's review and where to find detailed analyses; environmental justice analyses specific to each subpart are discussed in the RIA and supporting materials.
